grclanker v0.1.2 updates the FedRAMP tools to the October 2026 Consolidated Rules and moves the `sandbox-runtime` backend to sandbox-runtime 0.0.78. The tool surface is unchanged: `grclanker tools` still reports 241 domain tools and 7 compute backend tools.

## FedRAMP

- **October 2026 Consolidated Rules.** The FedRAMP docs are regenerated from rules version `2026.10.13.01`. `FRC-CSX-MOT` is gone, leaving 245 requirements. The CLI fetches the official rules at runtime, so `v0.1.1` already returned the October rule text. The changes below are new.
- **`fedramp_get_requirement`** shows each requirement's notification forms, mapped Rev5 controls, upstream note, and full update history.
- **`fedramp_search_frmr`** matches control IDs in requirement search, as KSI search already did, so `ra-5` finds the vulnerability detection and response rules.
- **Trust-center scaffolds.** `fedramp_generate_ads_bundle` and `fedramp_generate_ads_site` add the `FRC-CSO-JSN` hosting requirements to their READMEs and approval checklist: `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and CORS.
- **Cache.** The first run after upgrading discards FedRAMP caches written by older versions instead of serving them for up to 24 hours.

## sandbox-runtime backend

- **sandbox-runtime 0.0.78**, up from 0.0.61. On Linux, it mounts placeholders over protected files that do not exist yet, such as `.bashrc` and `.gitconfig`. grclanker handles them: `grep` no longer fails when ripgrep skipped only those placeholders, `find` leaves them out, and each sandboxed command is released when it exits, so no empty placeholders stay behind in the project.
- **`env exec` and `env smoke-test` exit when done.** On this backend, a successful run printed its result and then never exited. Both commands now reset the sandbox and exit.

## Runtimes

- **Cursor Agent SDK on `@cursor/bdk` 0.2.26**, up from 0.2.21. `zod` is now a CLI devDependency, because bdk 0.2.24 made it a peer dependency. The project still serves all 241 tools: 199 read-only tools and 42 approval-gated writers.

## Docs and site

- **grclanker.com runs on Next.js with Fumadocs.** URLs are unchanged. Search covers every docs page, every spec, and the CLI, Specs, and About pages.
- **Docs for phones.** Wide tables stack into labeled cards on narrow screens, and the hand-written docs are rewritten in shorter paragraphs. The generated FedRAMP pages get real paragraph breaks and a single title heading.

## Security

- `npm audit` is unchanged from `v0.1.1`. The CLI has 2 high advisories, both GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv in `node-forge`, counted once directly and once through `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`. No patched `node-forge` exists yet. The site has none.

## Upgrade notes

- Rerun the installer to upgrade. Settings and runtime state under `~/.grclanker/agent` are kept.
- Source checkouts should rerun `npm --prefix cli ci`, since the CLI lockfile changed.
- On the `sandbox-runtime` backend, an allow-listed hostname that resolves to a loopback, link-local, or cloud metadata address, or to one of your machine's own addresses, is now refused. Intranet hostnames on private ranges still work. To allow a refused address, add the IP address itself to `network.allowedDomains`.

Full changelog: [What's New](https://grclanker.com/docs/changelog/) and [v0.1.1...v0.1.2](https://github.com/ethanolivertroy/grclanker/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2).
